summary: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit reported that Storm-2139 members scraped exposed customer credentials from public sources and used them to unlawfully access accounts with generative-AI services. Microsoft also described a network of creators, providers and users supplying guardrail-bypass tools and enabling illicit AI services; Axios independently reported Microsoft's attribution. Microsoft’s civil action enabled website seizure. It reported later retaliation against counsel and planned criminal referrals. The clerk entered default against three defendants in December 2025. A magistrate recommended default judgment and permanent relief in May 2026; later public docket indexes list a grant.

assessment_boundaries: Microsoft's allegations and civil-enforcement positions are attributed to Microsoft; VIGIL does not adjudicate liability.

Credential theft and guardrail bypass do not by themselves establish Capability-Authority Separation, Target and Scope Authority Binding, Required Control Activation or Required Governance Routing without evidence of the provider's relevant authority or control-state mechanism.
The record remains unclassified under VIGIL even though the cyber-abuse occurrence itself is well evidenced.

The public Microsoft civil default-judgment record treats particular well-pleaded allegations as admitted for that proceeding. It does not disclose a complete per-request provider-side logging trace proving which content filter activated, which routes were skipped or whether a protective effect failed within an operative service control.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit reports that Storm-2139 members exploited exposed customer credentials scraped from public sources to unlawfully access accounts with generative-AI services and operated a network of creators, providers and users supplying tools for violating synthetic-content generation. Axios independently reports Microsoft's attribution. The evidence strongly establishes hostile credential abuse and service circumvention as attributed by Microsoft, but it does not establish an action-linked authority-conversion decision or a specific governance-control transition sufficient for a Fidelity mapping. Fresh court records distinguish the December 2025 entry of default from the May 2026 magistrate recommendation. The recommendation applies the default procedure to pleaded facts and seeks permanent injunctive relief. Later public docket metadata reports a grant, but the final order text was unavailable in this review. A recommendation is not itself the final judgment, and no criminal conviction or damages award is inferred. Source-first reinspection of the May 2026 court report and recommendation distinguishes the tool's attempt to prevent prompt revision, detection of policy rejection, and a proxy that modified traffic before forwarding to Azure endpoints. The default-judgment record describes Microsoft's allegations and deemed-admitted facts, not a published per-request filtering/control-state trace; that limitation is decisive for assigning a route-bypass versus insufficient-operating-control failure.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The record demonstrates an important boundary between threat activity and failure taxonomy. Stolen credentials can make an attacker look technically authenticated while leaving actual actor, purpose and authority invalid. That creates a governance requirement for credential-compromise detection, principal binding and abuse monitoring, but hostile access alone does not prove that an AI or governance process used credential possession as sufficient permission for the attacker’s actor, purpose and scope in the class-specific sense required by Capability-Authority Separation or Target and Scope Authority Binding. The separate authority-conversion candidate remains unresolved. The observed acquisition of working customer credentials now supports a distinct custody finding. Independent external assessment retains an evidentiary boundary for lifecycle security under foreseeable misuse: the attributed credential abuse establishes the attack and account access, but does not resolve the source-defined adequacy of provider protections when valid customer credentials were stolen. This does not determine liability or supply a missing taxonomy mechanism. Microsoft reports that Storm-2139 acquired exposed customer credentials and used them to access generative-AI accounts unlawfully. That establishes custody outside the authorised customer holders. The court’s procedural outcomes are not used to determine the custody result. The tool-assisted safeguard circumvention at the content generation stage is sufficiently material for explicit unresolved classification review even though the currently missing control activation and routing evidence prevents a definitive new class failure. E002 is no longer represented as a completed no-classification finding. The separate credential theft/access use recognised under the existing authentication-material custody class remains independently classified at E001.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This incident shows why VIGIL should not collapse a security threat taxonomy into a governance-failure taxonomy. The occurrence can be highly material while remaining unclassified when public evidence establishes attacker conduct but not the internal mechanism by which a governed system crossed a VIGIL class boundary. A positive allegation of guardrail circumvention should not disappear into an unqualified no-classification disposition when the unsatisfied class question is the exact control-state mechanism; preserve unresolved source-linked candidates and test the required-route and operative-control pathways separately.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Present source-backed material actions and later responses in supported relative order. Separate runs, source attributions and unknown ordering remain explicit. The November source-first reassessment distinguishes the material E002 content-protection uncertainty from the independently adjudicated E001 stolen-authentication-material mechanism; E002 is tracked as an unresolved class-fit question rather than mislabelled a completed nonmapping.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Microsoft reported that Storm-2139 creators made de3u software, providers used an oai reverse proxy, and end users produced prohibited synthetic images through Azure OpenAI. A May 2026 court report, summarising the civil First Amended Complaint in default proceedings, describes de3u trying to prevent Azure prompt revision and detecting content-policy rejections while the reverse proxy altered traffic and forwarded requests to Azure service endpoints. The reported tools enabled circumvention and illicit generation; the published excerpts do not identify one complete request-to-control activation and decision trace.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The harmful generation and traffic alteration are material, but a proxy that forwards requests into Azure does not itself prove that an obligatory governance route was avoided. The independently relevant distinction is between (a) skipping a mandatory checkpoint and (b) a provider filtering or abuse control operating but producing an inadequate effect. Microsoft's reported bypass does not establish which technical control state and pathway applied to a particular harmful request; default-judgment pleadings are not an authenticated raw Azure control trace.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Scope/target transposition is adjacent, but the evidence establishes attacker layering rather than an affirmative transposition of a valid provider grant.

The provider reports attempted circumvention and generated prohibited outputs, but the source does not show whether the relevant required control failed to activate versus activated with an inadequate effect. Preserve this as a mechanism differential, not an accepted activation failure.

The de3u/reverse-proxy combination changed request traffic, but the published account expressly says the proxy forwarded it to designated Azure endpoints. The source does not identify a mandatory Azure protective checkpoint that the harmful request bypassed rather than a checkpoint it passed through unsuccessfully. The required-route, alternate-route and missing effect conditions cannot yet be adjudicated.

Microsoft describes applicable Azure content filtering/abuse protection, a tool designed to block prompt revision or detect rejections, and prohibited imagery generated with the modified request route. The court report identifies the controls as integrated at service level, but not whether the applicable filter validly became operative on a specific harmful request, what protective action it performed, or the exact inadequacy relative to the protected purpose. The class's operational-activation and actual-effect conditions therefore remain unresolved; harmful output alone cannot certify the control mechanism.

clauses.adjudication_note: Material unresolved mechanism: Microsoft reports tool-assisted evasion and harmful synthetic generation, and the court's default-judgment record describes prompt-revision interference and altered proxy requests. It does not provide the session-level mandatory checkpoint/route, the valid activation state of filtering or abuse-detection, or the response/action on the request that produced a prohibited image. Existing current classes could cover a bypassed mandatory route or inadequate operative protective control, but a specific recognition condition remains unverified. No new taxonomy class is proposed and the existing unrelated stolen-credential finding remains decisive.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: All twelve dimensions reviewed against the bounded occurrence. Microsoft reports exposed credentials scraped from public sources and actual unauthorised access to generative-AI accounts. This is meaningful bounded misuse of protected account credentials. Provider attribution remains explicit. Later website seizure is containment, not proof that all copies or compromised accounts were restored. No broader sustained sensitive-data loss supports S4. Relational-role and heightened-protection boundaries independently tested; no new relationship is admitted. The additional content-control uncertainty is an interpretive gate on control mechanism, not evidence of a new harm dimension or changed magnitude. All twelve dimensional findings and overall S3 were independently retained.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The attributed stolen-credential access and guardrail circumvention directly engage secure functioning under foreseeable misuse. Microsoft establishes the hostile access and describes enforcement action, but the public report does not resolve whether credentials were exposed by the service or customers, which preventive safeguards operated, or whether the remaining risk was unreasonable under Section 1.4(a). Successful authentication with stolen credentials alone does not resolve that broader security-adequacy proposition.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: Microsoft's account of stolen credentials and illicit access to a generative-AI service directly raises the OECD secure-functioning/foreseeable-misuse benchmark even though no FC-derived candidate is admitted.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The authenticator-protection proposition requires secret authenticator content to be protected against unauthorised disclosure and modification. The observed secret disclosure/acquisition or custody-changing modification was unauthorised. Microsoft reports exposed customer credentials scraped from public sources and used for unlawful AI-account access. These were working customer secrets, not intentionally public identifiers. This is a bounded retrospective comparison with the selected control proposition, not a claim of certification or an independently binding historical duty.
